summary: Implemented patch::write_chart_edits<W: Write + ?Sized> with shared planning and complete preflight splice validation, direct writes from borrowed input slices, typed error chaining, and seven integration tests. All required final checks pass.

commands.outcome: Passed; formatted implementation and new tests.
Passed, exit 0: 165 existing unit tests and 7 integration tests; 0 doctests.
Initial run failed, exit 101: reversed_empty_ranges on the deliberately malformed 8..4 test span. Replaced it with an explicit std::ops::Range { start: 8, end: 4 } value; no lint suppression.
Passed after the test spelling correction.
Final run passed, exit 0: 165 existing unit tests and 7 integration tests; 0 doctests.

design_decisions: The caller retains ownership of the writer; a mutable borrow and Write + ?Sized support both concrete writers and dyn Write. The writer is neither flushed nor closed.

Both public chart editing paths call the same plan_chart_edits helper and validate_splices validator. Validation retains the existing range-error precedence and stable insertion ordering, checking all ranges and overlaps before the first writer call.

The streaming path sends unchanged input slices and existing owned replacement fragments directly through write_all. It never constructs the complete resulting XML. Existing structural fragment allocation remains in the planner.

WritePatchError owns the original PatchError or io::Error. Display provides context and Error::source exposes the typed original cause; custom I/O payloads survive unchanged. PatchError gains an Error implementation without changing existing variants or public construction.

write_all preserves short-write, Interrupted, and WriteZero behavior. Permanent I/O failures stop output immediately and may leave a prefix, explicitly documented separately from the untouched-writer guarantee for validation failures.

Existing function signatures, enum variants, public structs, inline tests, dependencies, and configuration remain intact. New tests cover every ChartEdit variant, mixed edits, same-offset appended series, direct borrowed no-edit input, byte preservation, late range and overlap rejection, late planner rejection, trait objects, and writer error behavior.
limitations: Validation is the existing mechanical edit validation; data must be scanned from the same XML as documented by the existing API.
This is an isolated component implementation, not a full document-engine or visual validation.
No allocation benchmark was run. The streaming memory behavior is supported by implementation inspection and a no-edit pointer-identity test, not invented allocation metrics.
I/O errors intentionally provide no rollback guarantee.
